## Project listing and filtering

The new `ona_projects` data source lists the projects in the organization, so a project no longer has to be looked up by ID.

```hcl
data "ona_projects" "by_repository" {
  remote_uris = ["https://github.com/example/repo"]
}

data "ona_projects" "most_popular" {
  sort = {
    field = "popularity"
    order = "SORT_ORDER_DESC"
  }
  limit         = 10
  include_count = true
}
```

- Filter with `search` (case-insensitive across project name, ID, and repository name), `project_ids`, `runner_ids`, `runner_kinds`, `remote_uris` (exact match on the git initializer's remote URI), and `creator_ids`. A project must match every filter that is set, and any value within a list filter.
- Results default to `id` ascending, which is creation order and stays stable between runs. Set `sort` to order by `popularity`, which the API recomputes periodically.
- All pages are fetched automatically. `limit` stops fetching once that many projects are collected.
- `include_count` returns the API's bounded total in `total_count`, and `total_count_relation` says whether that total is exact or a lower bound.
- Each entry in `projects` has the same attributes as the `ona_project` data source.
